papers.title: Cangrelor versus crushed ticagrelor in acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock (DAPT-SHOCK-AMI): a randomised, double-blind trial.
papers.summary: DAPT-SHOCK-AMI was a double-blind trial in 605 patients with acute myocardial infarction complicated by cardiogenic shock, comparing intravenous cangrelor with crushed oral ticagrelor. Cangrelor reached the platelet reactivity target at the end of primary PCI in 100% of patients analysed versus 22% with ticagrelor. The 30-day composite of death, myocardial infarction or stroke was 38% versus 41%, and non-inferiority was not demonstrated (P=0.13). Major bleeding was 6% versus 5%.

papers.title: Multimodality Cardiac Imaging Substudy of the DAPT-SHOCK-AMI Randomized Trial: Echocardiographic and Cardiac Magnetic Resonance Assessment of Cangrelor versus Crushed Ticagrelor in Cardiogenic Shock Complicating Acute Myocardial Infarction.
papers.summary: This prespecified imaging substudy of DAPT-SHOCK-AMI used serial echocardiography (208 patients) and cardiac MRI (93 patients) to compare cangrelor with crushed ticagrelor in cardiogenic shock after myocardial infarction. Acute microvascular obstruction was less likely with cangrelor (adjusted odds ratio 0.27), while infarct size did not differ. At one year, LVEF recovered more with cangrelor on echo (37.9% versus 21.7% of the acute value) and MRI (15.8% versus 2.1%). The substudy was not separately powered, so the findings are hypothesis-generating.

papers.title: Long-Term Survival After Initial Invasive or Conservative Management of Stable Coronary Disease in Patients With Advanced Chronic Kidney Disease: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND.
papers.summary: ISCHEMIA-CKD EXTEND followed 777 patients with advanced chronic kidney disease and moderate or severe ischemia, randomised to an initial invasive or conservative strategy, for a median of 8 years. All-cause mortality was 57.4% with the invasive strategy versus 56.8% with the conservative strategy (adjusted HR 1.05; 95% CI 0.87 to 1.28), and cardiovascular mortality was 40.3% versus 38.4%. There was no long-term survival benefit from initial invasive management.
papers.study_type: Long-term follow-up of a randomised trial

papers.title: High Bleeding Risk and Aspirin Omission at the Time of Primary PCI in STEMI: A Post Hoc Analysis of the PREMIUM Trial.
papers.summary: This post hoc analysis of the PREMIUM trial, which compared prasugrel monotherapy with prasugrel plus aspirin DAPT in 2,189 STEMI patients undergoing primary PCI, asked whether high bleeding risk changes the effect of omitting aspirin. 35.9% were high bleeding risk, with more ischemic events (16.2% versus 6.2%) and major bleeding (10.9% versus 4.9%). The effect of aspirin omission did not differ by bleeding risk (P for interaction 0.51), so high bleeding risk alone should not guide upfront omission.
papers.study_type: Post hoc analysis of a randomised trial

papers.title: Low-Voltage Area Ablation for Persistent Atrial Fibrillation: The COAST-AF Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: In the COAST-AF trial, 508 Canadian patients with persistent atrial fibrillation received pulmonary vein isolation with or without low-voltage area ablation. Recurrence did not differ significantly overall (49.4% versus 57.5%; HR 0.82; P=0.11). In the 268 patients with low-voltage areas, recurrence was lower with added ablation (49.3% versus 69.2%; HR 0.77). Safety was similar.
papers.short_title: the COAST-AF trial of low-voltage area ablation for persistent atrial fibrillation

papers.title: Iron Repletion in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: The IRONMET-HFpEF Randomized Trial.
papers.summary: IRONMET-HFpEF randomised 65 patients with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction and iron deficiency to single-dose intravenous ferric derisomaltose or placebo. At 12 weeks, peak oxygen uptake rose 1.2 mL/kg/min with iron and was unchanged with placebo (difference 1.1; P=0.02). Walk distance and NYHA class also improved; the Kansas City questionnaire score did not differ.
papers.short_title: the IRONMET-HFpEF trial of intravenous iron

papers.title: Statin-Ezetimibe Combination Therapy versus Statin Monotherapy in Atherosclerotic Cardiovascular Disease: A Prespecified Secondary Analysis of the Randomized Ez-PAVE Trial.
papers.summary: This prespecified secondary analysis of the Ez-PAVE trial randomised 3,048 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease to initial statin-ezetimibe combination or statin alone. Three-year major events were similar (8.5% versus 7.9%; HR 1.07; P=0.596), though combination therapy achieved lower LDL cholesterol (53 versus 62 mg/dL with intensive targeting). Safety was similar.
papers.study_type: Prespecified secondary analysis of a randomised trial
papers.short_title: the Ez-PAVE trial of statin-ezetimibe combination therapy

papers.title: Implementation of Single-Pill Combination Therapy Through Team-Based Care for Hypertension Control in Resource-Constrained Settings: A Cluster Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: This cluster randomised trial in 40 primary care clinics in Colombia and Jamaica enrolled 1,706 adults with uncontrolled hypertension. Team-based care with single-pill combination therapy lowered systolic blood pressure by 19.1 mm Hg versus 9.0 mm Hg with standard care at 18 months (difference -10.1). Control reached 69.5% versus 29.2%; serious adverse events were similar.
papers.short_title: single-pill combination therapy for hypertension in Colombia and Jamaica

papers.title: Dapagliflozin for Renal Protection in Heart Transplant Recipients: A Randomized Clinical Trial.
papers.summary: The DAPARHT trial randomised 430 heart transplant recipients to dapagliflozin 10 mg or placebo for 12 months. Dapagliflozin improved the eGFR slope: the change from 2 weeks to 12 months was 2.0 versus 0.3 mL/min/1.73 m2 (difference 1.7; P=0.03). There were no unexpected safety signals, and adverse events, including infections, were similar.
papers.short_title: the DAPARHT trial of dapagliflozin in heart transplant recipients

papers.title: Leveraging AI-ECG Technology for Early Notification and Tracking of AF Development (LATENT): A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.summary: The LATENT trial randomised 14,665 adults without prior atrial fibrillation to AI-ECG-guided Holter monitoring or usual care. New AF, flutter or pre-AF findings were more frequent with AI-ECG in monitored high-risk patients (0.74% versus 0.48%; P=0.046), but the result was statistically fragile, changing to P=0.057 if one event was reclassified.
papers.short_title: the LATENT trial of AI-ECG for atrial fibrillation detection

papers.title: AI-Identified Reasons for Nonescalation of Lipid-Lowering Therapy for Secondary Prevention.
papers.summary: This retrospective study used a large language model on clinical notes from 13,810 patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease and above-goal LDL cholesterol. Lipid-lowering therapy was not escalated in 88.7% of notes. The most common documented reasons were patient-reported adverse effects (12.6%), LDL close to goal (6.9%) and patient preference (6.8%).
papers.short_title: AI-identified reasons for not escalating lipid-lowering therapy
